newsitem.title: UK: Nickel to hit $8,000 in 4th qtr as demand expands.
newsitem.headline: Nickel to hit $8,000 in 4th qtr as demand expands.

text.p: Nickel prices are set to return to challenge levels in excess of $8,000 a tonne by the fourth quarter of 1997, broker Rudolf Wolff said in its latest Nickel Update.

It sees the market's strength coming from expanding demand, encouraged by the continued growth in the global economies, particularly in the developing world, and from the expansion in stainless steel production.
On the London Metal Exchange (LME) the three months delivery nickel price is currently trading around $7,400 a tonne.
Wolff said the high level of scrap utilisation seen in the first half of 1997 is expected to ease towards the end of this year, as supplies begin to tighten and the discount to the LME narrows.

Despite concerns of possible stainless steel production cutbacks due to high stocks, nickel demand is likely to benefit from new mill capacity coming on stream, particularly in South-East Asia, which will be looking to establish market share.
In addition, western world economies are predicted to grow by 4.4 percent in both 1997 and 1998 which is expected to underpin all industrial metals over the nex 12 months.

On the nickel production side Wolff sees some expansion, helped by planned increases at Russia's Norilsk complex, but not enough to match consumption growth and the market should be running into deficit in second half 1997.
